evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep jumps straight into 'I'll need a couple of pieces of information just so I can get you the right rate' with no time-box or 'quote you can depend on' framing, and never waits for a yes.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves directly from gathering addresses into logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Covered: property type (house), floor/stories (one story), rooms (two bedroom), walking distance (10 feet), big items (washer/dryer, freezer), box count (30 boxes). Missing: additional rooms beyond two bedrooms, special considerations beyond items being moved.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Asked as 'approximately how many boxes' — customer responds 'Just guess, and I'd say thirty.' Not framed as a typical-count overflow check.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Range given ($505–$606 for 1:30–2:00 slot; $660–$762 for 8:00–8:30 slot) but no personalization to customer's stated concerns (elderly, heat sensitivity, minimal items due to selling furniture).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee disclosed ($150 for morning Garland location), but no 2.5-hour-minimum or 15-minute-increments commitment framing; no explicit 'not a guess' language. Rep does mention '2.5 hour minimum' once when adjusting estimate but doesn't frame it as part of the pricing transparency upfront.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. Rep says 'So the minimum we have a two and a half hour minimum' and immediately pivots to options without pausing for customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Mentioned: 'we have our no re damage coverage that's gonna cover-up to $2,000 worth of incidentals.' Missing: no-deductible and no-fine-print framing; coverage presented vaguely as covering 'incidentals' rather than fully transparent terms.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No version of 'Does that put those to rest?' asked. Rep moves from damage coverage mention to confirming email without looping back.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Asked as 'Did you have any other questions for me that I can answer?' — a generic throwaway, not a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Customer volunteers 'why don't we do that and I'll go ahead and book it' — rep accepts this but never proactively asks 'Would you like our help with your move?'
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: arrival window (8:00–8:30 AM after customer change), confirmation email being sent, date (October 5). Missing: phone number confirmation restate, crew size, note left for crew about customer concerns (elderly, heat sensitivity).

top_strength: Rep gathered all four core discovery items (name, moving day, route, size) cleanly and maintained good rapport, with the customer feeling comfortable enough to ask follow-up questions and change preferences mid-call.
coaching_note: Section 1 is missing the quid pro quo framing entirely — start every call with 'This will take 10–15 minutes and you can walk away with a quote you can depend on. Does that sound good?' before moving into probing, and Section 2 never asks 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?' which skips the entire agenda-setting that makes the rest of the call targeted.
